summary: Describes a Same-Origin Policy requirement for RPKI Repository Delta Protocol servers and clients. Applying it to client and server communication isolates delta and snapshot files from different repository servers, which reduces possible attack vectors. It updates RFC 8182.

plainLanguage.summary: An RRDP notification could previously point a client to files hosted by another repository, or redirect it there. This RFC requires every referenced file and redirect to remain at the notification file's origin.

questions: how to secure rpki repository delta protocol
what is the rrdp same-origin policy
why does rrdp need a same-origin policy
subtitle: RRDP references and redirects must stay on the Update Notification file's origin.

tldr.problem: RRDP did not explicitly prohibit cross-origin references or redirects, allowing one repository to cause clients and another server to consume extra resources.
tldr.mechanism: Servers and relying parties MUST apply a Same-Origin Policy to notification references and HTTP redirects, keeping the same scheme, host, and port.
tldr.outcome: This RFC updates RFC 8182; a relying party rejects a notification or session when the origin check fails.

today: RFC 9674 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 8182. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Cross-Origin Risk
sections.content:
The original RRDP specification did not explicitly forbid a cross-origin URI in an Update Notification file from pointing to a Delta or Snapshot file. It also did not specify how HTTP redirection should be handled.

One repository could therefore reference resources on another repository, raising resource use for clients and the referenced server. Cross-origin redirects could cause similar effects.
sections.plainLanguage: A repository could send clients to fetch files from another repository. That could make both the clients and the other repository do extra work.

sections.title: Requirements for Repository Servers
sections.content:
Repository Servers MUST ensure that snapshot and optional delta URI attributes have the same origin as the Update Notification file's URI. Same origin means the same scheme, host, and port.

A Repository Server MUST NOT redirect a client to a location with a different origin from that Update Notification file.
sections.plainLanguage: A server must keep its snapshot and delta addresses on the same scheme, host, and port as its notification file. It must not redirect clients to a different origin.

sections.title: Requirements for Relying Parties
sections.content:
A relying party MUST check that URI attributes in the Update Notification file have the same origin as the file itself. If not, it MUST reject the file and RRDP cannot be used; implementations SHOULD log the cross-origin referral.

A relying party MUST NOT follow a redirect to a different origin while downloading notification, delta, or snapshot files. If the check fails, the RRDP session MUST be rejected and RRDP cannot be used. Implementations SHOULD log cross-origin redirects.
sections.plainLanguage: A relying party checks each address and redirect before using it. If one leads to another origin, it rejects the file or session and should record the reason.

sections.title: Deployment and Security
sections.content:
The RFC reports that its review of rpkiviews archives found one RRDP server using a same-origin HTTP redirect during April to September 2024. It observed no RRDP servers using cross-origin URIs in Update Notification files from October 2021 through October 2024.

The RFC concludes that the policy does not make commonly used RRDP operations non-compliant. It addresses an oversight that could let one repository operator increase resource use for others and their clients.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC's review found no observed cross-origin notification references in the period it examined. The rule addresses the extra resource use those references could cause.
